speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis results indicate the presence of red blood cells, white blood cells, and numerous bacteria, suggesting a significant infection. Given your right flank pain and these findings, do you currently have a fever or chills? REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture and Sensitivity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal readings from your recent measurements do not appear clinically relevant to your urinary symptoms, so I need to focus on your systemic signs. Do you have a temperature above 38°C (100.4°F), or are you experiencing shivering and nausea? REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture and Sensitivity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal measurements suggest your systemic status is stable so far. Since the urinalysis confirmed infection but we are waiting on the culture results, have you noticed any visible blood clots in your urine or pain when urinating? REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture and Sensitivity.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal readings confirm you are currently stable, but we need to pinpoint the source of the infection. Has the pain radiated to your groin, and do you have a history of kidney stones or recent trauma? REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture and Sensitivity. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal urine culture and renal ultrasound are unexpected given the initial findings of pyuria and hematuria; do you have a history of recurrent infections, recent antibiotic use, or any specific occupational exposures? REQUEST TEST: CT KUB with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT KUB with contrast: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.

The CT KUB confirms multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts without obstruction, which explains your history of hematuria, right flank pain, and recurrent pyuria despite negative cultures for active infection. This congenital anomaly predisposes patients to stone formation and bleeding due to calcium oxalate precipitation in the dilated ducts.
